blocks.text: Watch a video about SSL/TLS Inspection Policy (shows legacy UI).
SSL/TLS Inspection policies are used to perform scanning of the SSL/TLS traffic based on the source and destination of the traffic.
The SSL/TLS Inspection policies provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Simplify the deployment and ongoing operations of SSL/TLS Inspection.
Address the compliance and operational environmental requirements.
Inspect traffic for malware and data loss.
Allow, block, or restrict tenants.

blocks.text: Zscaler provides the following predefined special rules which you can enable or disable based on your requirements.
These rules are not editable and can only be implemented as is.

blocks.item: Zscaler-Recommended Exemptions rule: Predefined rule to automatically exempt known destinations that cannot be SSL/TLS inspected. This rule is enabled by default.

The Zscaler-recommended exemptions URL category contains a few dozen destinations that cannot be SSL/TLS inspected for various reasons, such as certificate pinning. This list also includes Zscaler-owned domains.

To discover the traffic that is not getting SSL/TLS inspected due to this rule, you can search the weblogs using the SSL/TLS Policy Reason field for the reason Not inspected because of Zscaler best practices. The percentage of traffic that matches this rule is commonly very small and less than 1%.

While it is recommended not to inspect these domains, you can always disable the rule with the Edit option. Alternatively, you can leave the rule enabled, but create higher-order inspect rules if you want to inspect only specific domains outside the list.
O365 tenant restriction inspection rules: Predefined rules to enable Office 365 Tenancy Restrictions for location and remote user traffic.

O365 One Click rule: Predefined rule, controlled by the Microsoft-Recommended and Legacy Office 365 One Click setting. You can modify the Rule Order, Admin Rank, Rule Status, Rule Label, Description, and choose Evaluate Other Policies (i.e., URL Filtering and Cloud App Control) or Bypass Other Policies under the Do Not Inspect action for this rule and cannot edit other attributes. To learn more, see Configuring SSL/TLS Inspection Policy.

If Evaluate Other Policies is selected and a block (or similar) rule exists in the URL Filtering policy, Cloud App Control policy, or other policies, then the system allows these rules to match the SSL/TLS bypassed traffic. However, with the SSL/TLS bypass, the policy application is limited due to the lack of decryption. This would mean that subsequent policy action is likely limited to only the domain portion and not the full URI. For example, for the website sample.com/chatBotAI, only sample.com is seen. So, users can access sample.com, and it's classified under IT Services, and do not separate the fact that sample.com/chatBotAI is classified under General AI and ML Applications.
UCaaS One Click rule: Predefined rule, controlled by the UCaaS One Click configuration.

Unauthorized Traffic Bypass for IoT Classifications rule: Predefined rule to allow unauthorized traffic to bypass SSL/TLS Inspection for IoT classifications in all IoT policy-enabled locations. This rule is disabled by default and cannot be deleted. You can modify the Rule Order, Admin Rank, Rule Status, Rule Label, and choose Evaluate Other Policies or Bypass Other Policies under Do Not Inspect Action for this rule and cannot edit other attributes. You can enable this rule to temporarily allow unauthorized traffic to bypass SSL/TLS Inspection, so that Zscaler AI/ML can classify devices.

blocks.heading: About the SSL/TLS Inspection Policy Page

blocks.text: On the SSL/TLS Inspection Policy page (Internet Access > Policy > SSL/TLS Inspection), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View the recommended SSL/TLS Inspection policy.
See image.
Add an SSL/TLS Inspection rule.
Filter the SSL/TLS Inspection rule by Rule Label.
Search for an SSL/TLS Inspection rule.
Modify the table and its columns.
See image.
View a list of all SSL/TLS Inspection rules. For each SSL/TLS Inspection rule, you can view:
Policy Rule Details
Rule Order: The order of the rule. SSL/TLS Inspection rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order. You can sort this column.
Rule Name: The name of the rule. You can sort this column.
Admin Rank: The admin rank of the rule. You can sort this column.
Rule Action: The action configured for the rule.
Rule Label: The label of the policy rule, if available.
Source IP Groups: The source IP groups of the rule, if available.
URL Categories: The URL categories of the rule, if available.
Cloud Applications: The cloud applications selected for the rule.
Destination Groups: The destination groups of the rule, if available.
Forwarding Gateways: The forwarding gateways of the rule, if available.
ZPA Application Segment: The Private Access (ZPA) application segment of the rule, if available.
Locations: The locations of the rule, if available.
Location Groups: The location groups of the rule, if available.
Users: The users of the rule, if available.
Groups: The groups of the rule, if available.
Departments: The departments of the rule, if available.
Devices: The devices of the rule, if available.
Device Groups: The device groups of the rule, if available.
Remote Users with Kerberos: The remote users with Kerberos of the rule, if available.
Device Trust Level: The device trust level of the rule, if available.
User Agent: The user agents of the rule, if available.
Endpoint Applications: The endpoint applications of the rule, if available.
Endpoint Application Tags: The endpoint application tags of the rule, if available.
Endpoint Application Risk Level: The endpoint application risk level of the rule, if available.
Description: The description of the policy rule, if available.
Edit, duplicate, or delete an SSL/TLS Inspection rule.
The SSL/TLS Inspection rules are paginated with up to 500 rules displayed per page.
